result.title: What Does an Observability Foundation Model Know?
result.comment: Accepted to NeurIPS Main Conference '26. 25 pages
result.summary: A linear probe can show that a label is recoverable from a model's hidden states, but not whether that goes beyond what the input already reveals, or whether the model uses it. We audit Toto, an observability forecasting foundation model, on the Benchmark of Observability Metrics (BOOM) across five series-disjoint resplits, comparing linear probes on its frozen residual stream with models that read the raw input window and with Toto's architecture stripped of its trained configuration. Short-vs-medium cadence and metric type are more linearly recoverable from Toto's residuals than from the strongest raw-window model in every resplit (macro-F1 0.766 vs. 0.633 and 0.545 vs. 0.498). Domain is nearly tied, and series cardinality is recovered far better from the raw window. MOMENT-base shows related cadence, metric-type, and domain readouts. Recoverability is not use: exchanging Toto's residuals with those of high-burst donors moves a future-burstiness readout as intended but does not make forecasts consistently burstier than a randomized donor. A BOOM-trained coordination probe has negative zero-shot R^2 on the tested external benchmarks. We report each label against its strongest baseline.

AI.brief_summary: 本文审计可观测性预测基础模型 Toto 的隐藏状态：在 BOOM 基准上比较线性探针与原始输入窗口模型的标签可恢复性，并做残差替换与协调探针实验，发现可恢复性普遍高于输入基线，但探针可解码并不等于模型实际使用该信息。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「可解码≠被使用」的探针审计框架，与 LVR 关心的答案是否真正使用 latent 内容、视觉旁路与信息坍缩高度同构，可供核查其残差替换/零样本探针设计能否迁移到 VLM 的 THINK/LOOK/STOP 贡献分配与证据筛选评价。
